submitted.rationale: Index 10 (Ba 0.528) gave 5.46e-5 A, the highest of the three merit measurements. That is about 16x index 8 (Ba 0.498, 3.32e-6 A), and index 14 (Ba 0.61) gave 0. The models point to the same Ba-rich side of BaMnO3: 2H-BaMnO3 is on the MACE hull with a predicted gap of 2.73 eV, and Ba6Mn5O16 has a moderate gap of 1.99 eV, so a mixture of the two could absorb 3.22 eV light and make photocurrent.

rejected.reason: Measured 0 A. Ba3Mn2O8 is predicted to have a 3.07 eV gap, but no photocurrent came from this region, and its XRD matched none of the candidate phases well.
Neighbouring phases such as Ba2Mn3O8 (0.34 eV) and BaMn4O8 (0.89 eV) have near-metallic gaps, so they are poor photoanodes.

consultations.verdict: Support: Ba3Mn2O8 (Ba 0.6) is on the MACE hull (0.006 eV/atom) with HSE gap 3.07 eV, just below the 3.22 eV photon energy, so it can absorb while keeping a wide gap. Index 14 (Ba 0.61) is closest. The XRD match is ambiguous, so this measurement is a test.

Support: 2H-BaMnO3 (mp-19156) is on the MACE hull (0.001 eV/atom), and its predicted gap is 2.73 eV, below the photon energy. The XRD at index 14 matched it best (0.44). Index 8 (Ba 0.498) is closest to this stoichiometry. BaMnO4 (gap 3.53 eV) would not absorb, so it is not the target here.

Mildly supportive. On the Mn-rich side of BaMnO3, the neighbouring phase Ba2Mn3O8 has a predicted gap of only 0.34 eV, which is metallic-like and a poor photoanode. On the Ba-rich side, Ba6Mn5O16 has a moderate gap of 1.99 eV. So Ba 0.53 (index 10), a BaMnO3/Ba6Mn5O16 mixture, is the better-motivated neighbour of the measured nonzero point at 0.50. Ba 0.61 already gave zero, so I am not going further Ba-rich.
